registered_before: any counterfactual outcome was computed; the October 21 behavior audit's associations were already known and motivated the rules
question: Had each live position alert's condition closed the whole remaining position, would the October 2025-26 long option trades have kept more money than the actual exits, and does the alert's timing beat an exit at a random minute of the same trade?

population.trades: closed or expired long option trades (buy_to_open entries, sell_to_close exits) opened 2025-07-10 to 2026-10-19, the behavior audit's dataset
excluded_and_counted: holding window longer than 10 calendar days (path metrics' limit)
no cached Alpaca option minute bars covering the trade window
fills that do not allocate first-in-first-out
population.not_extracted: trades opened after 2026-10-19 are kept for the prospective evaluation and are not read by this run

position_accounting: actual fills applied in time order, first in first out; at a rule's trigger every remaining contract is sold at the exit price and later fills (adds or exits) are dropped; return on premium divides by the premium of the entries made before the trigger
marks: position gain = realized + open contracts x bar close x 100 - entry premium, on regular-session 1-minute trade bars; a bar holding a fill is not judged (minute fills cannot be ordered within their bar), as in trade_path.option_position_path

execution.fill: open of the next bar that exists within 5 minutes, before the actual final exit; otherwise the rule does not apply to that trade and the actual exit stands (counted)
execution.cost_base: sell at the bar open less 3% of price, minimum $0.01 per contract share (half of an assumed 6% bid/ask spread; historical option quotes are not available)

rules.giveback: the live alert's thresholds: armed at a bar close with gain >= 10% of entry premium and >= $50; fires at the first later bar close with gain <= 3%
rules.hold_hour: the live alert's clock: the first bar close at least 60 regular-session minutes after the first entry (an entry before 09:30 counts from 09:30), on the entry day only
rules.expiry_day: the live first expiry alert: the first bar close at or after 90 minutes before the close on the expiration date (14:30 ET; 11:30 ET on 13:00 closes)

outcomes.primary: total dollar difference, counterfactual minus actual, over every trade in the population (untouched trades contribute 0)
secondary: mean difference in return on premium (percentage points) over the trades a rule touched

random-exit comparison: for each touched trade, 200 exits at uniformly random judged minutes between the first judged minute and the actual final exit (seed 20261024); timing value = rule difference minus the random exits' mean difference on the same trades
outcomes.uncertainty: 2,000 bootstrap resamples by trading day of entry (seed 20261024); Bonferroni across the 3 rules: 98.33% two-sided intervals for primary decisions

periods.independence: neither period is untouched: the rules' thresholds came from the audit, which read both. A positive check half is consistency, not confirmation

decisions.supported_saving: primary 98.33% interval above 0, each period's dollar difference above 0, each period's return-on-premium difference above 0, and still above 0 at the stress cost
decisions.timing_informative: supported_saving and the timing value's 98.33% interval above 0

outcomes.supported_saving and timing_informative: eligible for prospective testing as an exit trigger
outcomes.supported_saving only: investigate further: the money is in exiting sooner, not in the alert's moment
outcomes.interval includes 0 or periods disagree: reject as a demonstrated saving; the alert may still help as a reminder, which this cannot test
outcomes.primary interval below 0: reject: following the rule mechanically would have cost money

limits: trade prints, not bid/ask midpoints; the live alert marks at the midpoint
a mechanical exit is not what an alert does: the alert asks for a decision, so these are bounds on full compliance, not the alert's effect
dollars are dominated by position size; the return-on-premium difference is the size-neutral check
no counterfactual re-entry: after a rule exit the trade is over
prospective: the same code and constants, frozen at this commit, applied to trades opened from 2026-10-20; reviewed once at 30 touched trades for the give-back rule or 2027-01-29, whichever comes first, with no change of thresholds before then
